definition: A small model from a fourth family, used across 3 sources as an additional cross-family point where two families would leave a trend underdetermined. Its appearances: one of 18 checkpoints in a cultural-knowledge audit, one of the models in a cross-family steering audit spanning five families and 0.6B to 72B, and a backbone for representation-based exploration. Its role is the same in each -- a claim established on Llama and Qwen is checked here, and the archive's related material is full of cases where such a check narrows or reverses the result.

evidence.note: Builds a parallel entity grid of 27 folk-narrative motifs across 10 cultures and instruments 18 models with probing, logit lens, activation patching and generation, finding that the residual stream separates cultures cleanly in every model while the readout collapses onto Greco-Roman defaults — so the failure is at the decoder, not the encoder.
evidence.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs

evidence.note: Audits four neuroscience-inspired claims about language models across 17 checkpoints from five families and 0.6B to 72B, and shows that an apparent emergence of concept steerability with scale is produced entirely by uncalibrated measurement -- raw intervention units, the readout metric, and a fixed operating point -- with correcting any one of the three removing the trend.
evidence.title: When Is a Steerable Concept Representation Real? Measurement Confounds in a Cross-Family Audit of Neuroscience Parallels in LLMs

evidence.note: Uses elliptical bonuses over a language model's own hidden-state representations as a diversity signal, validates it in a clean inference-time selection setting, then transfers the same signal into RL post-training — where it eliminates the diversity collapse that degrades pass@k at large k.
evidence.title: Representation-Based Exploration for Language Models: From Test-Time to Post-Training

name: Phi-4
